pages.title: What Is Waste?
pages.content:
Waste is any material that people do not want anymore. Usually, it is what is left after we have used the useful parts of something. However, the idea of zero waste looks at waste in a different way. From this point of view, waste is not just something left over. It is the result of poor product planning and the way we consume things. The basic idea of zero waste is to stop making rubbish as much as we can.

Some numbers show how serious the problem is. In 2023, the world produced 2.3 billion tons of city waste. Experts expect this number to reach 3.8 billion tons by 2050. At the same time, only 62 percent of city waste is treated in proper waste facilities.

Food and other organic materials make up the largest part of city waste. Paper, cardboard and plastic follow closely. As countries become richer, their waste also changes. The fast rise in plastic waste is especially worrying because huge amounts of it end up in oceans and rivers. City waste also contains many other materials, and each one needs its own way of collection and recycling.

pages.title: Paper and Wood
pages.content:
Paper comes from forests. Recycling paper is important because it saves a great amount of raw materials. It is also valuable for the economy.

Paper waste is collected separately from other waste so that it does not get wet. Then it is pressed into blocks, which makes it easier to transport. In recycling facilities, the old paper is processed and turned into new paper and cardboard products.

Wood comes from trees, and we use it every day in furniture, packaging and buildings. It is also an important material for carrying and protecting many kinds of products. Recycling centers turn wood waste into useful timber and boards. In this way, the wood can be used again instead of being thrown away.

vocabulary.definition: Natural materials that are used to make products.
To push hard on something to make it smaller or flat.
To carry people or goods from one place to another.
To treat a material in a series of steps to change it.
Thick, strong paper used for boxes.
Wood that is ready for building or making things.

pages.title: Plastic
pages.content:
Plastic is a basic material in many of the products we buy, and a lot of manufactured goods contain it. However, there are different types of plastic, so they cannot all be recycled in the same way.

Between 2000 and 2019, global plastic production almost doubled. It rose from 234 to 460 million tons, an increase of 97 percent. During the same period, plastic waste grew even faster. It rose from 156 to 353 million tons, an increase of 126 percent.

So what happened to all this plastic waste at the end of its life? Only 9 percent was recycled, and 19 percent was burned in waste facilities. Half of it, 50 percent, went into landfills. The other 22 percent was left in open dumps, burned in the open air or escaped into nature. Most of this plastic ended up in rivers, lakes and seas.

vocabulary.definition: Products that are made in factories.
Of the whole world.
The process of making something, or the amount that is made.
To become two times bigger.
A large area where waste is buried under the ground.
A place where people leave waste without control.
To get out of a place.

pages.title: Glass and Composite Packaging
pages.content:
Glass is made mainly from sand, soda ash and limestone. Bottles and jars become glass waste when we finish using them. Glass waste is collected in special containers and sorted by color. This helps to keep the quality of recycled glass high. After that, the glass is melted again and made into new bottles and jars. This reduces the use of raw materials and lowers carbon emissions.

Composite packaging is made by combining paperboard and plastic, and often a very thin layer of aluminum. It is widely used for juice and milk cartons, and for this reason it creates a huge amount of waste. Composite waste must be collected separately. Then it is processed in advanced facilities, where these layers are separated from each other. After that, these materials are recycled or used to make new products.

vocabulary.definition: A white or gray rock that is used in building and glass.
Something that you keep things in, like a box or a bin.
To put things into groups by type, size or color.

pages.title: Metal and Vegetable Oil
pages.content:
Metal is produced from minerals that are found in the Earth. Aluminum drink cans, oil cans and tomato paste cans are all metal waste. Metal waste must be collected separately so that it can be recovered. After it is collected, the metal is melted and used to make new products. This process needs much less energy than mining new metal and processing it.

Vegetable oils are made from plant seeds that contain a lot of oil, such as olives, sunflowers, corn, cotton, soybeans and canola. Used frying oil, solid fats and oil that is past its expiration date are all vegetable waste oil. This oil must be collected separately because it can pollute our water. Special facilities then turn it into biodiesel, a clean and renewable fuel.

vocabulary.definition: A natural material, such as iron, that comes from the ground.
To get back something useful.
To dig into the ground to get metal or coal.
The date after which you should not use a product.
To make air, water or land dirty and harmful.

A fuel for vehicles that is made from plant oil.

pages.title: Organic Waste
pages.content:
Organic materials play an important role in our daily lives and in farming. As a result, we produce both animal and plant waste. Fruit and vegetable scraps, as well as wheat, barley and rye straw, are all examples of organic waste.

Food waste is a serious part of this problem. About 13.2 percent of the world's food is lost after it is harvested, before it reaches the customer. Another 17 percent is wasted in homes, restaurants and shops.

Where does most food waste happen? Surprisingly, the answer is our own homes. In fact, 61 percent of all food waste happens in households. This means that each of us can make a real difference.

vocabulary.definition: To be part of something and have an effect on it.
Small pieces of food that are left and not eaten.

To collect crops from the fields.

To have a good effect on a situation.

pages.title: Electronic Waste and Batteries
pages.content:
Electronic devices make our daily tasks much easier at home, at school and at work. When we throw away dishwashers, washing machines, fridges, vacuum cleaners, toasters, computers or mobile phones, they become electronic waste. This waste must be collected in separate bins, so that its toxic substances can be removed safely. Then the devices are taken apart into smaller pieces. In this way, valuable materials like metals, plastics and rare elements can be recovered.

Batteries are devices that store energy in chemical form and change it into electrical energy. When they reach the end of their life, or when they are damaged, they become waste batteries. Waste batteries must be collected in special bins because their dangerous chemicals can leak into the soil and water. Then special facilities safely take out important metals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel, so that they can be used again.

As we have seen, recycling recovers many valuable materials. However, it still needs a lot of energy and effort, so recycling alone cannot solve the problem. This is where Zero Waste comes in. Instead of only managing waste, it tries to stop waste before it is even created.

pages.title: What Is Zero Waste?
pages.content:
When you hear the words "zero waste," you might think they mean producing no trash at all. But that is simply impossible! We all use products and create waste every day. So what does "zero waste" really mean?

The Zero Waste approach is based on the main idea of sustainability, which means meeting our needs today without damaging the resources that future generations will need. By following this approach, people use resources wisely and produce as little waste as possible. It also encourages people to make and use things responsibly: they avoid waste, reuse items and recycle. This way of thinking supports eco-friendly habits. It also asks us to think about the whole life of a product, from beginning to end. As a result, nothing is wasted, and people start to see leftover materials as something valuable.

Every year, people produce between 2.1 and 2.3 billion tons of waste. This means we are throwing away valuable resources. These resources could easily go back into the economy, and then we would need fewer new raw materials. Waste pollution is also harmful to our health and to the economy. It makes climate change faster, and it causes many plants and animals to disappear.

vocabulary.definition: The physical or mental energy that you need to do something.

pages.title: The Circular Economy
pages.content:
Zero Waste is seen as an important bridge to a circular economy. A circular economy aims to stop waste and pollution by keeping products and materials in use for as long as possible. In simple words, it works like nature, where nothing is wasted and everything is used again and again.

It is called "circular" because resources do not move in a straight line from the factory to the landfill. Instead, they move in a loop, and old products are turned into new ones. The main goal is to make sure that economic growth does not harm nature.

The circular economy is the opposite of the traditional linear economy. A linear economy follows a simple "take, make, waste" model. Resources are taken from nature, used, and then thrown away.

vocabulary.definition: Moving in a circle.
Something that connects two things or ideas.
To try to do or achieve something.
A shape like a circle, with no beginning or end.
An increase in size or amount.
Moving in a straight line, from start to finish.

pages.title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
pages.content:
Zero Waste is built on three main principles of the circular economy.

Reduce: The aim is to stop waste before it starts. We do this by using fewer resources and buying only what we really need.

Reuse and Repair: Products should be designed to last a long time, so that people can use them again and again. To do this, products should be durable, easy to repair and easy to upgrade. Repairing means fixing things when they are broken or damaged. It helps products last longer, and it also saves money.

Recycle and Upcycle: This principle tries to keep products and materials in the economy for as long as possible. We can do this by collecting and recycling waste, or by designing products that are easy to take apart and reuse. Recycling means turning waste into new materials and products. It sends less waste to landfills and saves natural resources. Upcycling goes one step further: it turns waste into new products of higher value.

vocabulary.definition: A basic rule or idea.
To plan how something will look and work.
Strong and able to last a long time.
To make something better or more modern.
Turning waste into a product of higher value.
How useful or important something is, or how much money it is worth.

pages.title: Why Is the Circular Economy Important?
pages.content:
The circular economy has several key benefits.

Less waste and pollution: The circular economy reduces the total amount of waste and pollution. Products and materials stay in use for a long time. As a result, we don't need to take as many new resources from nature or make as many new products.

Better use of resources: The circular economy uses resources more efficiently. It uses fewer materials from the start, and it reuses and recycles as much waste as possible.

Sustainable growth: This approach also helps the economy grow in a sustainable way. It lowers the cost of getting rid of waste, and it creates new jobs in recycling and reuse.

In short, the circular economy is a promising new way of thinking about the economy. It can reduce waste and pollution, help us use resources better and support sustainable growth. As we move toward a more sustainable future, it will become more and more important.

vocabulary.definition: A good result or advantage.
Working well without wasting time, money or energy.
To throw away something that you don't want.

pages.title: Waste and Climate
pages.content:
The way we manage waste is closely connected to the climate crisis. For this reason, Zero Waste is a powerful way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. When organic materials rot in landfills, they release methane, a very strong greenhouse gas. Because of the way we produce and consume, global greenhouse gas emissions have more than doubled in the last 50 years. Zero Waste keeps resources out of landfills, so it stops these harmful gases at the source.

Better waste management during the whole life of products can cut global greenhouse gas emissions by 15 to 20 percent. However, there is a serious injustice. Many developing countries produce very low emissions, but they often suffer the most from climate change, such as terrible disasters and rising sea levels.

Good waste management also reduces air pollutants like methane and black carbon. These come from leaving waste in open areas and burning it.

A gas in the air that keeps heat in and makes the Earth warmer.
To become soft and bad, like old food.

pages.title: How Can We Help?
pages.content:
The best waste is the waste that is never created. That is why we need to act before waste appears. Here are some practical ideas.

We can reduce food waste with good training and smarter shopping in canteens, restaurants, hotels, hospitals and homes. Packaging-free shops and local markets offer fresh food, and they help to stop both packaging waste and food waste. Most single-use packaging is not really necessary. Take-away coffee cups, food containers, plastic water bottles and plastic straws can all be replaced with waste-free choices.

vocabulary.definition: Useful and easy to do in real life.
Made to be used only once and then thrown away.
To use one thing instead of another.
A place in a school or factory where people eat meals.
Sold without boxes, bags or wrapping.

pages.title: Cities, Families and the Future
pages.content:
Local governments can also play a big role. They can set up refill systems for drinks, support reusable diapers and make sure that waste-free hygiene products are sold in local stores. For things that last a long time, like electronics, furniture and clothes, they can support second-hand shops and reuse platforms, both in town and online. Cities can also encourage paperless offices and set up tool libraries, where people borrow tools instead of buying them.

These ideas are easy to put into practice. In the end, teaching children and their families about Zero Waste is the best way to change our wasteful habits. And there is no better time to start than now.

The main rule of consumption is to reduce waste. Reducing waste on both a personal and global scale is possible through zero-waste and sustainable practices, which leads to a more livable world. Zero Waste is a way of thinking, not a final result. A waste-free society is not a place where we arrive and stop. It is a journey that continues.

In a world where we consume too much, we need to remember Gandhi’s wise words: “The world has enough for everyone's need, but not enough for everyone's greed.”
